text:
Asha Patel: heads-up — the bootcamp sample app is hitting a weird JSON-mode + function-call issue when auth retries fire. saw this during the live lab just now. :facepalm:
Liam Chen: what does "weird" look like? runtime errors or bad outputs?
Asha Patel: runtime. model returns a function call payload, SDK attempts to parse it into the typed helper, then our retry path triggers the function call again and the JSON parser complains about 'Extra data after top-level value'.
Samir Rivera: hmm that sounds like double-append to the stream buffer. Is this on JS or Py SDK?
Asha Patel: user was following the JS bootcamp sample (github.com/redwood-inference/bootcamp -> sample-fncall). using JS SDK v0.9.1. The Python demo didn't hit it in the workshop, but could be parity gap.
Liam Chen: can you paste the minimal client snippet you used?
Asha Patel: sure — here's the essential flow we ship in the sample app:
```js
// simplified
const res = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'redwood-chat-1',
  json_mode: true,
  function_call: { name: 'create_ticket', arguments_schema: ticketSchema },
  input: prompt
});
// on network error we retry with auth-refresh
if (isAuthErr) await auth.refresh();
const retry = await client.responses.create(...)
```
Samir Rivera: ok. if the first call streams partial JSON then the retry appends a new streaming sequence into the same parser buffer, the JSON-mode validator will see: <json><json> and blow up.
Asha Patel: exact error from console: "SyntaxError: Unexpected token } in JSON at position 245 — Extra data after top-level value"
Liam Chen: quick mitigation: add an idempotency token at requests.create (client supports idempotency_key) so retries are routed server-side rather than re-sending/duplicating streaming frames. for the bootcamp sample we should teach this pattern.
Samir Rivera: also we should harden the SDK parser: when json_mode is enabled and a retry happens due to auth, the SDK should reset the streaming parser state before reattaching. otherwise parity issues will vary across runtimes.
Asha Patel: agreed. for triage: can we (1) patch the sample app to use idempotency_key + note in README, (2) file a small SDK bug to reset parser on auth-retry, (3) add an e2e test for JS+Py parity?
Devex Bot: New issue created: DEVEX-1412 — "JSON-mode parser state not reset on auth retry (causes double-function-call parse errors)" https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/DEVEX-1412 :white_check_mark:
Liam Chen: devex-1412 is great. I'll pick the SDK fix (JS runtime parser reset) and add a regression test that simulates an auth 401 in the middle of a stream.
Samir Rivera: I'll update the bootcamp repo with idempotency example + a small note about "if you implement custom retry logic, always reset/tear down streaming parsers".
Asha Patel: thanks. can we also add a short blurb in the onboarding quickstart about using idempotency_key for long-running tool calls? new folks tripped on this in the session.
Liam Chen: yes — will PR to docs after the SDK patch. ETA tomorrow for the fix, then sample app follow-up.
Asha Patel: awesome. saved my demo :) :thumbsup:
Samir Rivera: FYI we should consider exposing a helper in the SDK: client.responses.createWithRetrySafe(...) that wraps idempotency + automatic parser reset. reduces onboarding friction.
